name: Shuup
title: Shuup SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce Connector
description: Svelte Commerce on Shuup: 19 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in; coupons, reviews, pages, countries, states and wishlist are gaps.
lede: Solid core coverage for a smaller API: cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Shuup’s REST API. Coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are the recorded gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are not.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Shuup shop

quickStartNote: The guide removes only `@misiki/litekart-connector`. A fresh clone’s `package.json` also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector`, and with two connectors installed and neither of them Litekart’s, the build stops and asks for `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR` — so this removes both.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL
env.note: Your Shuup shop’s URL. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: A JWT, sent as `Authorization: JWT <token>` — Shuup accepts neither `Token` nor `Bearer`.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_KEY
env.note: HTTP Basic username, used when no token is set; meant for server-to-server calls. See the limitations.

env.name: PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_SECRET
env.note: HTTP Basic password, with the username above.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/shuup-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_SHUUP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_SHUUP_ACCESS_KEY`, `PUBLIC_SHUUP_STORE_ID` and `PUBLIC_SHUUP_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Let the storefront’s origin make cross-origin requests to Shuup (CORS): in production the browser calls `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL` directly, not only the server.
howItWorks: Shuup’s REST API accepts HTTP Basic, session and JWT authentication. The connector sends a JWT as `Authorization: JWT <token>` — the header prefix Shuup’s JWT library expects — and falls back to HTTP Basic when it has a username and password instead.

Installing the package is the whole switch. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever `@misiki/*-connector` is installed, and `src/lib/core/connectors/init.ts` hands it every `PUBLIC_SHUUP_*` variable that is set, camel-cased, at boot — in the server hook for server rendering and in the client hook for the browser, which must reach the same URL in production.

There is no Litekart API behind the storefront here, so store identity — name, logo, currency, menus, plugin toggles, theme colours — comes from `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` merged under the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`. Until you override it, the store is called “Test”. Any Litekart REST path the connector still inherits is answered from that local data, or resolved empty, rather than requested.
limitations: CMS pages: not wired — legal and CMS pages render their layout with empty content.
Pages that depend on a service that is not wired render their empty state rather than failing.
If you set `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_KEY` and `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_SECRET` for HTTP Basic, those credentials reach every visitor: SvelteKit sends `PUBLIC_` variables to the browser.
Homepage sections other than the live product list come from the active theme’s static content — the standing rule for themes.
The Conversational Shopping assistant is Litekart-only; its widget stays hidden when another connector is active.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the shuup connector is active but PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/shuup-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “PUBLIC_…_API_URL is set, but it configures a different backend than the one this build runs on”
troubleshooting.fix: Another backend’s variable is still set, usually left over from the one you switched from. Remove it, or install that backend’s connector. `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL` is exempt: it only points the dev proxy.

troubleshooting.problem: The store is called “Test”, or shows the wrong name and logo
troubleshooting.fix: Store identity is static on this backend. Set `name`, `logo`, `currencyCode` and the rest in the default export of `kitcommerce.config.ts`; `src/lib/core/connectors/default-store.json` lists every field.

troubleshooting.problem: `[shuup] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Shuup has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

troubleshooting.problem: `http proxy error: api/... ECONNREFUSED` in dev
troubleshooting.fix: A Litekart REST path was requested from outside the connector, so its guard never saw it. Vite proxies `/api` to `PUBLIC_LITEKART_API_URL`, or to `localhost:7000`.

`@misiki/kitcommerce-core` declares it as a peer, and `vite.config.ts` redirects that specifier to whichever connector is installed. Make sure exactly one `@misiki/*-connector` is listed in `package.json`.

faq.q: Can I run a Shuup shop on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired; coupons, reviews, CMS pages, countries, states and wishlist are not. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Shuup shop.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Shuup?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/shuup-connector`, set `PUBLIC_SHUUP_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: How does the connector authenticate with Shuup?
faq.a: With a JWT, sent as `Authorization: JWT <token>`. Shuup does not install token authentication, so `Token` and `Bearer` headers are both refused. HTTP Basic is the fallback, meant for server-to-server calls.

faq.q: Has the Shuup connector been run against a real Shuup store?
faq.a: Not against a live production instance — no Svelte Commerce connector has been. It was written by reading Shuup’s authoritative API source, and the Svelte Commerce maintainers ask Shuup’s own maintainers for a sandbox to run it against.
